Validation_Type.reason: Confirmed. The design has two stages. (1) Signatures are trained on cognitively unimpaired (NL+SMC) versus AD, and their performance is estimated by 10 iterations of 10-fold stratified CV. (2) The frozen signatures are then applied to a separate group of EMCI and LMCI subjects who were not used in training, to predict 36-month conversion. Table 3 labels these columns 'Test Set', as distinct from 'Internal Cross-Validation', and p.4 calls the step an independent verification. The core task (MCI-to-AD conversion, the registry's own T2) is evaluated only on this held-out partition. That is k-fold plus a held-out test partition, which is V3. V2 ('no separate test set') is contradicted by the paper. It is not V4: the test subjects, and the second VGF confirmation cohort, all come from ADNI-GO/ADNI-2, the same consortium as the training data.
Validation_Type.quote: Performance of the signatures derived from these algorithms for accurately classifying CUI versus AD subjects was estimated via 10 iterations of 10-fold stratified cross-validation ... These signatures were then applied to an independent group of EMCI and LMCI subjects at baseline to predict their future progression to AD within 36-months.
